title: test(plugin-view,plugin-list,plugin-calendar): drop the retired target key from three tree fixtures (objectui#8031)
body:
Fixes #8031

Test-only. Three `type: 'tree'` fixture fields drop the retired snake_case target key —
in `plugin-view`'s expand-gate suite, `plugin-list`'s relational-sort suite and
`plugin-calendar`'s expand-gate suite — plus one empty-frontmatter changeset declaring
that nothing releases. No renderer, no `detectParentField`, no sibling field touched.

## Every suite's verdict is unchanged, measured both ways

Same command before and after the edit, from the repo root, through the shared
serialisation lock:

```
pnpm exec vitest run --reporter=verbose \
  packages/plugin-view/src/__tests__/ObjectView.expandGate.test.tsx \
  packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.relationalSort.test.tsx \
  packages/plugin-calendar/src/__tests__/ObjectCalendar.expandGate-6453.test.tsx
```

| reading | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| summary | `Test Files 3 passed (3)` · `Tests 23 passed (23)` | identical |
| per file | plugin-view 8 · plugin-list 6 · plugin-calendar 9 | identical |
| test-name set | — | `diff` of the two sorted verbose logs is EMPTY |

`turbo run type-check` for the three packages (each runs `tsc --noEmit` and then
`tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the edited test programs are in it): 19 tasks
successful, 19 total. `check-changeset-presence`, `check-control-bytes`,
`check-new-cross-file-line-citations`, `check-test-path-roots` and
`check-governed-queue-guard --test` all exit 0; the last prints
`NOT GOVERNED — 4 path(s) checked`.

## Why DROP and not rename — re-measured on the installed copy

`@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, `FieldSchema.safeParse`, with a nonsense key as the
negative control:

| input on a `tree` field | verdict |
|---|---|
| no target key (what this PR leaves) | ACCEPT |
| retired snake_case target key | REFUSE — `unrecognized_keys` **plus** a rename hint |
| nonsense key `zz_nonsense_key` | REFUSE — `unrecognized_keys`, **no** hint |
| declared `reference`, this object's own name | ACCEPT |
| declared `reference`, another object's name | ACCEPT |

The hint is attached to a refusal, not to an acceptance — the card's two-directional
measurement reproduces at 17.4.0. On the read side `detectParentField` has read only
the declared spelling since objectui#6837 half 2, and the list sort picker's
object-def branch reads only that spelling too. So the key was refused by the schema
and read by nobody, and a refused key annotates nothing: renaming it would turn a
refusal into an ACCEPTED self-annotation these fixtures never made.

## Three premises corrected — read this before reusing the card's framing

1. ⚠️ **These three are NOT foreign-target.** Each container declares an object
   identity and the retired key already named exactly it: `TASK_SCHEMA` is `task` and
   the field named `task`; the relational-sort suite's object def is `contacts` and
   the field named `contacts`; `VISIT_SCHEMA` is `visit` and the field named `visit`.
   What made these three refused is the SPELLING, not the target. The card's title,
   its "whose target names another object" framing, and its disposition clause "none
   of these three containers declares an object identity a self-reference could name"
   are all false of these three. The disposition survives the correction; the
   classification does not.
2. ⚠️ **The seven instances are therefore not indistinguishable.** objectui#7839's
   four were target-foreign or identity-less (three of them declare no object at all;
   the fourth declares `deal` and named `deals`). These three are target-self. What
   unites all seven is an inert, parse-refused target key on a `tree` field, which is
   what the shared disposition rests on.
3. ⚠️ **"A shape the spec refuses at parse" is true upstream, not of the installed
   pin.** Row five above: a declared `reference` naming another object is ACCEPTED at
   17.4.0. `refuseForeignTreeReference` landed on objectstack `main` after this pin
   was cut, exactly as objectui#7839's own suite docblock records.

A fourth correction is the card's line number for the `plugin-view` fixture, which the
dispatching seat had already caught: every address was re-derived on today's `main`.

## The shape scan was re-run, and it found a fourth emit — reported, not touched

Re-run as a shape scan rather than a key grep: every `type: 'tree'` emit in the tree
(single- and double-quoted, template literals, JSON spellings, every file extension,
constants holding the string, and field factories that take the type as a parameter).
31 literal emits. Of those, three are these fixtures; two carry a declared target that
names the DECLARING object (legal self-references in `plugin-tree`); the deliberate
foreign arms in objectui#7839's own suite are that suite's subject and must stay; the
rest carry no target or are view entries rather than field defs.

⭐ One emit is invisible to BOTH sweeps and is a live instance of the card's own
lesson: `packages/app-shell/src/utils/expandableFamily.identity-5874.test.ts` builds
its fields through a factory that takes the type as an argument and attaches
`reference: 'accounts'` to every one of them, including the `tree` member
`parent_node` on an object named `deal`. A grep for the key sees a helper with no
tree in sight; a grep for the emit sees no literal type at all. It is NOT in this
PR's scope and NOT the same disposition — the target there is load-bearing
(`expect(out.referenceTo).toBe('accounts')` reads it), so dropping it would go red.
It is handed back for triage in the report, with dedupe words.

## The pin — a truthful "not soundly pinnable here"

The population-shaped gate the card asks for ("no `type: 'tree'` emit carries a target
naming another object") is writable but not soundly: I have a counterexample in hand.
A gate keyed on literal emits would go green on the app-shell factory above, and that
green would read as "the population is closed" — the exact false closure the card's
own lesson names, repeated one level up. Judging "names another object" also needs the
declaring object's identity, which in a hand-built fixture is an arbitrary neighbouring
constant a scanner would have to guess at. The sound route is a type-level one — type
these fixtures against the spec's own field type, so the compiler refuses the retired
key and the tree arm — and that is a separate change, not something to smuggle in
under a test-only card. ⛔ A pin that re-asserted these suites' existing assertions
would measure nothing, so none was added.

## Acceptance notes

- **To file (handed back, not filed here — this seat does not open cards):** the
  app-shell factory emit above. Dedupe words: `expandableFamily.identity-5874`,
  `field('tree')` factory, foreign tree target, `resolveActionParams` `referenceTo`,
  tree-emit enumeration blind spot.
- **Noted, not filed:** at the parse door the retired spelling is refused on a
  `lookup` too (measured), so "dead on a `tree` field only" is about the READERS, not
  about `FieldSchema` — several app-shell readers still read the snake spelling for
  the lookup family, which is why the sibling lines are legitimately load-bearing and
  untouched. Carrier: the next card that moves the lookup-family spelling reads this;
  no PR is pending on it today.
- `Clause-②: no` — three hand-built test fixtures. No symbol exported, removed,
  renamed or retyped, no published `.d.ts` member and no accept set moves. Measured,
  not inferred from a diff grep: the three files sit under `src/__tests__/`, which
  every published tsconfig excludes from the emitting program (enforced by
  `pnpm check:published-tsconfig-exclude`); each container is a module-local `const`;
  all three packages ship `dist` only; the diff adds zero `export` lines and deletes
  one property from an object literal whose own annotation already declares that key
  optional.
